COMSC School Handbook 25 26
Section 13 Getting started 


13.1 Hybiau 
You'll find new student Hybiau opening across our campuses including a local Hyb for your 
discipline. We've invested in these student spaces to give you easy access to the support you 
need and provide collaborative study space to build your university community. We can't wait 
for you to start using them. 
During the start of this academic year Hybiau will be getting up and running to deliver a whole 
range of support and services. We'll be in touch soon to tell you more about what you can 
expect. In the meantime, please follow the welcome information from your school and enjoy 
the start of your university life at Cardiff! 
Hybiau is the plural form of Hyb in Welsh (pronounced huh-bee-eye).

COMSC School Handbook 25 26
Section 13.2 Student ID Card 


13.2.1 Collection and Usage 
All students must collect their Student ID card within the first two weeks of the academic year. 
Cards are available from the Centre for Student Life on Park Place and must be collected 
before borrowing any equipment provided by the School. 
Your Student ID card is essential for: 
- Accessing computing labs and other school facilities 
- Borrowing equipment from the School office 
- Using University libraries, including borrowing books 
- Entering school buildings outside teaching hours

COMSC School Handbook 25 26
Section 13.2.2 Card Updates 
You must carry your Student ID card at all times while on campus. Staff or security may 
request to see it, and failure to present a valid card may result in being asked to leave the 
premises.

13.2.2 Card Updates 
Student ID cards must be updated every 30 days. Update points are located: 
- Outside Room 0.19 (Ground Floor, Abacws) 
- On the accessibility door to Room 3.36 (Third Floor, Staff Room) 
To update your card, hold it against the panel until the blue light turns green. If you encounter 
any issues with updating or using your card, please visit the Facilities team in Room 0.20 or 
email Abacws@cardiff.ac.uk.

COMSC School Handbook 25 26
Section 13.3 Accessing additional IT support 
If you have an IT problem or query, please contact the IT Service Desk, which offers 24-hour 
IT support, seven days a week: 
 
 Email: Send queries or support requests to it-support@cardiff.ac.uk. 
 Telephone: For immediate assistance, call +44 (0)29 2251 1111 (available 24/7). 
 
Find out more about IT services and support here. 
 
Help and advice about online safety and to support you in identifying phishing emails is 
available on the intranet. 
 
Remember: Cardiff University will never email you asking you to validate your email 
account or to warn you that your mailbox is full! Please contact the IT Service Desk for 
further information. 
 
Shortly after you first enrol, you will be given guidance on the use of the school's computing 
facilities. Information on the School's systems and software can be found here. In the 
Documentation section, you will find a selection of documents describing the school's facilities 
and how to use them. If you require further help using the systems in the laboratories, you 
should contact the IT service desk or speak to the school's IT support team. 
 
Faults and maintenance requirements, including printer faults, jams and lack of toner, should 
be reported to the IT team via email IT-Support@cardiff.ac.uk. 
 
You will be able to use the school's PC labs for your own work outside of scheduled teaching 
sessions, though precedence should always be given to those who require specific equipment 
for coursework. Please Note: these labs are exclusively for the use of COMSC students only.

COMSC School Handbook 25 26
Section 13.4 Free Software 
As a Cardiff University student, you are entitled to install Microsoft Office on your home 
computer for free, and to continue using it for as long as you are a Cardiff University student. 
Other free software and information is listed here. Information on School-specific systems, 
software, services, and documentation can be found at COMSC SCHOOL ORG. It is strongly 
recommended that you install Microsoft Teams, Microsoft Office, Microsoft OneDrive, etc. on 
your computer.it-support@cardiff.ac.ukit-support@cardiff.ac.uk

COMSC School Handbook 25 26
Section 13.5 Raising Issues in Computer Labs 
Students requiring technical assistance within Cardiff University computer labs can contact IT 
Support through the following channels: 
- Email: Send queries or support requests to it-support@cardiff.ac.uk. 
- Telephone: For immediate assistance, call +44 (0)29 2251 1111 (available 24/7).

COMSC School Handbook 25 26
Section 13.6 Semester dates 
The teaching year is split into two teaching semesters, Autumn and Spring. There is also a resit assessment period in Summer. For postgraduate taught master's programmes there is also 
a Dissertation stage which follows completion of the taught period. 
 
Dates for the standard university periods can be found here. 
 
Please note that for joint programmes where COMSC is not the home school, the semester 
and dissertation dates may be different, and you should contact your home school for that 
information.

COMSC School Handbook 25 26
Section 13.7 BCS Membership 
BCS student membership brings immediate benefits such as support for their learning through 
regular webinars run by specialist groups and branches, access to the BCS library, and 
discounts and offers on items such as laptops. As BCS members, students sign up to the 
BCS professional code of conduct, designed to maintain ethical standards within the IT 
industry. On completion of their BCS accredited degree, graduates are eligible to apply for 
chartered and professional status, with continued access to an international network of IT 
professionals and experts, and support for their career progression though mentoring, industry 
engagement, professional skills development programmes and career development tools 
aligned with the SFIA framework.

COMSC School Handbook 25 26

Learning Central is the University's Virtual Learning Environment and is where the majority of

made available from the start of the semester on Learning Central. This will give you an 
overview for the entire semester workload to enable you to plan your work.

coursework instructions. If you are unable to submit your work on Learning Central due to

let us know by submitting a declaration of extenuating circumstances. You'll find more details

Section 14.4 Examinations 
Examinations are typically held online, via Learning Central. The exam periods and timetables 
can be found on the intranet. 
The exam timetables are published 6 weeks prior to the start of the autumn and spring exam 
periods (and 2 weeks prior to the resit exam period).

COMSC School Handbook 25 26
Section 14.5 Marking 
We aim to return all assessment marks within 20 working days of the submission deadline. 
If, for any reason, this timeframe cannot be met, we will inform students as soon as possible. 
All assessments are checked internally by appropriate academic members of staff before they 
are released to students. Assessments that contribute to degree classification (i.e. all but those

In Year 1 of undergraduate programmes) are also checked and approved by external 
examiners. 
Where a coursework assessment forms a substantial part of a module's assessment, a sample 
of the assessments for the cohort is reviewed by appropriate members of academic staff. 
 14.5.1 Provisional Marks 
Each module mark is composed of marks for individual assessments (components) specified 
in the module description. All marks are provisional until they have been confirmed by an 
Examining Board, which usually takes place at the end of the teaching year. As part of this 
process, the Board may decide to adjust marks for a module, this means that provisional 
marks you received previously could be subject to change. After the meeting of the Examining 
Board, you will be sent a transcript by the Academic Registry.

COMSC School Handbook 25 26
Section 14.5.2 Component and Module Marks 
You will receive marks for each individual assessment (component) on a module. Details of 
assessments can be found in the module description. The mark overall mark for a module will 
be calculated according to the weightings for each element of summative assessment, 
specified in the module description, rounded, and recorded as a whole number (see section 
2.5 of the Academic Regulations). 
You can fail a module's assessed component in two ways: 
- By obtaining a mark below the pass mark. The pass mark is 40% for undergraduate 
modules and 50% for postgraduate modules. 
- By submitting more than 24 hours late or not at all. 
Note: failing a module's assessed component does not necessarily mean you fail the whole 
module as the module mark is calculated from all assessed components.

COMSC School Handbook 25 26
Section 14.5.3 Resits 
If the Examining Board determines that you have failed no more than 60 credits in the 
academic year, you will be expected to resit modules you have not passed in the resit 
period. For further details, please see section 4.11 and 5.10 of the Academic Regulations. 
Resit assessments take place prior to the start of the following academic year. Resit 
coursework usually takes place in July and early August with exams and class tests taking 
place in the August resit period, dates of which can be found here. Your resit results will be 
confirmed by the Resit Examining Board, which is normally held in the first week of September, 
following which, academic transcripts and year results will be sent to you by the Academic 
Registry. 
If you have failed more than 60 credits during the academic year, you will not be eligible for 
resits in the August resit period. Depending on your results, you may be offered to repeat the 
year, or in some cases, will be asked to withdraw from your programme. For further details, 
please see section 4.14 and 5.13 of the Academic Regulations.

The type of reassessment you will need to complete depends on the components you have 
failed. You may be required to resit more than one component if there are multiple failed 
components for a module. The resit component will be the same type as the original 
assessment (e.g., exam, coursework, etc). 
At undergraduate level, you have a maximum of three attempts to pass a module. At 
postgraduate level, you have two attempts at a module. For further details, please see section 
2.10 of the Academic Regulations). 
If you fail modules in the resit period and are unable to progress to the next phase of your 
programme (see section 14.5.4), you may be offered to repeat the year, or in some cases, will 
be asked to withdraw from your programme.

COMSC School Handbook 25 26
Section 14.5.4 Progression 
Note: this simplified guidance is to be read in conjunction with the University's Academic 
Regulations. 
UG Students: 
Following the resit period, if you fail to pass up to 30 credits in a year, and have sufficient 
attempts left on the required modules, you may be allowed to progress and carry the module(s) 
into the following year (see Progression Rule 2 in section 4.8 of the Academic Regulations). 
These credits will be taken as an external student but must be passed before graduating with 
a degree. 
PGT (one year programmes): 
To progress from the taught part of the programme to the dissertation phase, you will need 
to attain 120 credits on the taught part of your programme.

progression rules apply to programmes within COMSC. 
CM2305 'Group Project' is a Required module for all second-year diets in which it appears. 
As it is a Required module, students cannot progress to their final year (or placement/year of

15.1 Student Voice - Student-Staff Panels 
Student-Staff Panels (SSPs) provide a formal channel for your student representatives to 
meet with staff and discuss issues related to your education. They also provide an opportunity 
for the school to consult with students and receive feedback on proposals. 
As a school, we're committed to working in partnership with you to make our community the 
best it can be. We want to listen to your concerns, make meaningful changes, and continue 
building a school we can all be proud of. Student-staff panels, to which your year and 
programme will be asked to elect representatives, are in place for both undergraduate and 
postgraduate students. Your Panel, which meets at least once each semester, reports directly 
to the School's Board of Studies (BOS) and the School Education and Student Experience 
Committee (SESEC), both of which have student representation. The Panel is accustomed to 
openly discussing any topic affecting students and will receive any representation from you, 
made via your year representative(s). The Chairs of both the UG & PGT Student Staff Panels 
also attend the School's BOS and SESEC, to discuss any high priority matters, which may 
need to be addressed by the school's senior management. 
 
You don't need to wait for a panel meeting to raise any concerns. If something is troubling 
you, please feel free to speak with your Student Representative, who can raise the issue on 
your behalf with the appropriate staff member (such as the Module Leader, Year Tutor, or 
Programme Lead) and communicate the outcome back to you. Alternatively, you can discuss 
the matter directly with your Personal Tutor. If you're unsure which route to take, the Student 
Services Team is always available to guide you. 
 
Details about your Student Academic Representative(s) will be shared with you by email. They 
will reach out to their peers directly for student feedback throughout the academic year.

Extenuating Circumstances Procedure for Taught and Undergraduate Students
Section 1 What are extenuating circumstances? 
An extenuating circumstance is: 
- severe and exceptional; and 
- unforeseen or unavoidable; and 
- close in time* to an assessment; or where you can demonstrate the 
circumstances continued to have an impact on you at the time of the 
assessment. 
 
Examples of extenuating circumstances are: 
- serious short-term illness or an accident 
- bereavement, i.e. the death of a close relative or friend, partner, or significant 
other person 
- significant adverse personal or family circumstances including severe financial 
issues 
- being a victim of a serious crime such as sexual assault, discrimination,

the assessment, or the content of your assessment has been impacted 
- evidence of a disability which has worsened or changed at the time of the

- evidence of a long-term health condition* which has worsened or changed at

text:
Cardiff University Extenuating Circumstances Procedure v2 09/25 
Examples of circumstances which are not extenuating are: 
- minor illnesses that typically would not cause you to take time away from 
study 
- poor time management e.g. where you have not given yourself sufficient time 
to complete the assessment by the deadline. You should allow sufficient time 
to upload assessments to University systems 
- assessment-related stress which is not diagnosed as an illness 
- where the event/circumstances declared were foreseeable or able to 
be anticipated, for example, planned religious festivals/events, jury duty, 
compulsory armed forces deployment, competing at international sporting, 
arts, or other civil responsibilities. There is separate information about how 
the University may be able to support your attendance at these types of events 
on the Intranet, please see the Planned Activity Guidance. If you are expected 
to take part in any of these events you should inform your School straight 
away 
- where the event/circumstances declared were foreseeable or able to 
be anticipated, for example, planned events, holidays, weddings, or other 
family-related events 
- where the event/circumstance is not close in time to the assessment 
- where the circumstances that you are declaring have already been addressed 
by reasonable adjustments 
 
If you are feeling well and functioning effectively, you should undertake all assessments 
and will not need to submit a declaration of extenuating circumstances. 
 
If you are not sure whether your circumstances are exceptional and meet the criteria for 
extenuating circumstances, independent advice and support in completing the 
declaration can be obtained from the Students' Union Student Advice Service.
policy_name: Extenuating Circumstances Procedure for Taught and Undergraduate Students

text:
Extenuating Circumstances Procedure for Taught and Undergraduate Students
Section 2 How to declare your circumstances 
If you experience severe and exceptional circumstances in the period immediately prior 
to, or at the time of, an assessment, you should submit a declaration* of extenuating 
circumstances*. You are usually expected to report extenuating circumstances in the 14 
days before the impacted assessment. 
 
In most cases, when you experience extenuating circumstances, you will be unable to 
complete the assessment as scheduled. You are responsible for managing your own 
personal circumstances and informing the University of any issues which you believe are 
having an impact on your studies before the deadlines in this Procedure. 
 
There are limited situations when you can submit a declaration of extenuating 
circumstances if you have started an assessment; you must therefore consider whether 
your circumstances are likely to prevent you from being able to engage effectively, before 
you attend or submit the assessment. 
 
You can declare your circumstances by completing the form available on this page of the 
Student Intranet.
policy_name: Extenuating Circumstances Procedure for Taught and Undergraduate Students

text:
Cardiff University Extenuating Circumstances Procedure v2 09/25 
If assessments are not completed on time and without extenuating circumstances, the 
penalty for late submission, non-submission or non-attendance will be applied as stated 
in the University's Academic Regulations. 
 
If you do not complete an assessment i.e. submit coursework or sit a timed-limited 
assessment*, because you have extenuating circumstances, you may be required to 
complete the assessment at a later time to attain credit, or equivalent for non-modular 
programmes. Your progress to the next academic year or the award of a degree may be 
delayed if you do not have sufficient credits, or the equivalent for non-modular 
programmes. If your programme is accredited by a Professional Statutory Regulatory 
Body (PSRB)* there may be additional factors which may impact your progression. 
Where appropriate, your School will explain these you. 
 
For every summative* assessment, you have one opportunity to declare your 
circumstances. If your declaration is rejected for not meeting the University's definition of 
extenuating, you cannot reapply for an extenuating circumstances remedy for the same 
assessment unless your circumstances have changed or worsened. 
 
If you re-declare in advance of the summative assessment deadline* for extenuating 
circumstances where an application has previously been rejected for that assessment, 
you may be asked to provide evidence* in support of your circumstances or their impact 
on you. Failure to provide evidence when requested will result in your declaration being 
rejected.

Extenuating Circumstances Procedure

- situations 1 to 4 refer to the situations in which you can declare extenuating

University's published guidance on Extenuating Circumstances in group work which is 
available on the Student Intranet. Declarations of extenuating circumstances are 
confidential* and will not be shared with other members of the group.

Extenuating Circumstances Procedure for Taught and Undergraduate Students
Section 4 What your School will do with your declaration of 
extenuating circumstances 
 
Decision Making 
Declarations* of extenuating circumstances* will be considered by the Extenuating 
Circumstances Group*, or a nominee of the Extenuating Circumstances Group who will 
have been trained in the Procedure. 
 
The Extenuating Circumstances Group, or their nominee, will consider your extenuating 
circumstances, any supporting evidence* and the remedy that you have requested. 
The Extenuating Circumstances Group, or nominee, will decide whether to approve or 
reject your declaration. Where your declaration is approved, the Group or nominee will 
confirm the remedy.

text:
Cardiff University Extenuating Circumstances Procedure v2 09/25 
The Extenuating Circumstances Group will meet regularly throughout the academic year 
to ensure that all requests received are considered in a timely manner. Where more than one academic remedy is available in the 'Situation' that you are 
declaring, the Group or nominee can make the final decision on what option is approved 
taking into consideration your circumstances and the remedy that you have requested. Your School will communicate a decision in relation to your circumstances as soon as 
possible. When you are declaring extenuating circumstances in advance of an 
assessment date or deadline*, this will usually be within seven days of the declaration* 
being made. For circumstances declared in advance of your assessment, if the declaration is 
submitted fewer than seven days before the assessment deadline*, you may not receive 
the outcome on your declaration before the assessment deadline. In this case, you will 
need to decide whether you are well enough to sit or submit the work. If you make an EC declaration before the exam start time and then decide to sit the 
examination: the decision to attempt the exam will override your extenuating 
circumstances declaration and the mark for your attempt will stand. If you make an extenuating circumstances declaration before the coursework submission 
deadline and then decide to submit your coursework: your submission will override your 
EC declaration unless: 
- your extenuating circumstances declaration is accepted (upheld); and 
- the School is able to offer you the opportunity to resubmit within a week of the 
original submission date (two weeks for part-time students) i.e. as though the 
extension had been granted before the coursework deadline. If you subsequently complete the assessment and are impacted by circumstances as 
described in situations 6 or 7, you still have the opportunity to declare extenuating 
circumstances after the assessment, with supporting evidence, to request an 
extenuating circumstances remedy.

Extenuating Circumstances Procedure for Taught and Undergraduate Students
Section 5 Examining Board Remedies 
Cardiff University Extenuating Circumstances Procedure v2 09/25

5 Examining Board Remedies 
The Extenuating Circumstances Group* will confirm to the Examining Board that actions 
have been taken in accordance with this procedure for students who have declared 
extenuating circumstances. 
 
The Extenuating Circumstances Group will report to the Examining Board: 
- students who have been permitted to defer* assessments; and 
- students who have declared extenuating circumstances* which have been 
accepted as being related to protected characteristics* (under the Equality Act 
(2010)), a long-term health condition*, or caring responsibilities*, and who have 
completed the assessment. 
 
The Examining Board will consider and, as appropriate, confirm one of the remedies 
below. Where more than one remedy may be of benefit to you, the Examining Board will 
explain the options to you, for you to choose the remedy: 
- where the pass mark was not achieved for the assessment or the module, allow a 
retake of the assessment element as a 1st attempt (or 2nd/3rd if you have failed 
previously) at the next available opportunity. 
- where the pass mark for the module has been achieved but the pass mark for the 
assessment element has not, offer you the opportunity to retake the assessment 
element as a 1st attempt (or 2nd/3rd if you have failed previously) or award 
credit for the module without further assessment. 
- where the module and assessment elements have been passed offer you the 
chance to retake the assessment element if at 1st attempt, or award credit for 
the module without further assessment. 
- if you have been awarded credit for a module without further assessment, the 
Examining Board may discount* module marks that have been affected by 
extenuating circumstances when calculating the final mark as specified in the 
Assessment Regulations.
policy_name: Extenuating Circumstances Procedure for Taught and Undergraduate Students

text:
Extenuating Circumstances Procedure for Taught and Undergraduate Students
Section 6 Academic Appeals Procedure 
If you have declared extenuating circumstances* which were rejected by the Extenuating 
Circumstances Group* or their nominee, the reasons for the decision will be provided. If 
you feel that the decision was unreasonable you can challenge this decision upon receipt 
of your results letter under the Academic Appeals Procedure. 
An academic appeal submitted under the ground of extenuating circumstances will need 
to be supported by evidence*. 
 
You have 28 days from the date of your transcript or results letter, which is sent by email 
at the end of the academic year, to make an appeal against the decision of the 
Examining Board.

text:
Extenuating Circumstances Procedure for Taught and Undergraduate Students
Section 7 Support from the University 
Please note, the University is not an emergency service. If you are experiencing a crisis 
that poses a serious risk to your health or safety, please call 999 to access emergency 
support from the appropriate services. If you are experiencing extenuating circumstances*, you may also benefit from 
accessing additional support from the University. The University's Student Life Services 
are available to all students of Cardiff University. The Student Life services are not able 
to prescribe medication. If you need help from a medical professional, you are advised to 
contact your GP or a local medical facility. Depending on your circumstances, you may 
benefit from speaking to the Student Life Services for advice from one or more of the 
following teams: 
- Student Support Intervention Team - The Student Support Intervention Team 
(SSIT) is a dedicated team of practitioners who provide confidential support 
and guidance for students who have been affected by: Violence, abuse or any 
other inappropriate behaviour that causes offence or distress; and/or urgent 
mental health needs or who are posing a risk to themselves or others. You can 
use Report + Support to self-refer into the SSIT. Your report will not be handed 
to your School as a declaration of extenuating circumstances* 
- Student Disability Service - The Student Disability Service are available to 
arrange Reasonable Adjustments* for the duration of your studies to help you 
to engage with your studies where you are managing a disability. Reasonable 
Adjustments* are different from the remedies available to you under the 
Extenuating Circumstances Procedure and can be requested under the 
Reasonable Adjustments Policy 
- Counselling and Wellbeing- Trained counsellors can provide support and 
advice for you if you are managing difficult personal circumstances or 
difficulties with your mental health and wellbeing 
- Occupational Health - Support from Occupational Health Practitioners who 
can identify adjustments to support your studies where you encounter health 
problems that impact on your ability to complete elements of your course.

Policy 
In cases where coursework is submitted late, and where there are no 
extenuating circumstances: 
- if the assessment is submitted no later than 24 hours after 
the deadline, the mark for the assessment will be capped at 
the minimum pass mark 
- if the assessment is submitted more than 24 hours after the 
deadline, a mark of 0 will be given for the assessment 
Long-Term 
Health Condition 
A mental or physical health condition that has impacted you, or is 
likely to impact you, for six months or longer and may not meet the 
definition of being a disability for the purpose of the Equality Act 
(2010). A long-term health condition is different to an injury. More than three 
different 
occasions 
Where the student has logged in to the appropriate portal to declare 
Extenuating Circumstances at three different times and for three 
different assessments.

Late Submission Policy
Section 1 As a research student, you are expected to submit your thesis within the 
regulatory timescale, as specified in the Research Degree Regulations. Your 
submission deadline may be extended only in accordance with the 
Extenuating Circumstances Policy (Research Students).

2 If you do not submit your thesis by your specified deadline (including in cases 
of resubmissions) and if you are not withdrawn from your studies, you may 
still be permitted to submit your thesis as a Late Submission.

text:
Late Submission Policy
Section 3 If you intend to make a Late Submission, you should request, via your School 
Director of Postgraduate Research, to delay the closure of your student 
record for a maximum of 12 months. Your School will instruct Education and 
Governance to update your student status.

4 If you are permitted to make a Late Submission, your enrolled status will be 
removed, subject to any appeal process and outcome, as you will be 
considered to be out of time.

to University buildings or events, other than as a member of the public.

Late Submission Policy
Section 7 The decision whether to accept your thesis as a Late Submission will be at 
the discretion of your Head of School: if you are out of time, it is not your right 
to have a Late Submission accepted. Factors that will be taken into account 
include the viability of the thesis, the currency of the work it represents, and 
the availability of staff to assess the thesis and oversee any required 
corrections after an examination.

Late Submission Policy
Section 8 Your Head of School may accept your thesis as a Late Submission no later 
than 12 months from your submission/resubmission deadline. If your thesis is 
accepted, you will be required to pay a Late Submission fee and to re-enrol 
with the University.

9 The Late Submission fee is equivalent to the submission fee charged to staff 
candidates and the resubmission fee charged to candidates who are invited 
to represent their thesis following a first examination, and is published 
annually.
